Use your largest, widest frying pan or a heavy sauté pan in place of the wok. It's needed in steps 2 and 3. Because a flat pan holds less, cook the chicken in 2 batches over high heat in step 2, adding a little of your vegetable oil (you have it in the pantry) for each batch, and set the first batch aside so the pan doesn't crowd and steam the meat. In step 3, stir-fry the broccoli and pepper for about 3-4 minutes, then return the chicken and add the soy sauce. The household has white wine vinegar, so use that for the acidity. Mix about 1 teaspoon (5 ml) of it into a ladle of hot chicken stock (about 100 ml), so it's gentler than neat vinegar, and add that to the rice. Stir until it's absorbed. The vinegar is sharper than wine, so don't add more, and taste at the end before adding any extra salt.

Use the white wine vinegar your household has. Stir in just 1 to 2 teaspoons (5-10 ml) along with a ladle of the hot chicken stock, since vinegar is much sharper than wine. It gives the same bright acidity, and the smell cooks off within a minute or so. Stir until the liquid is absorbed, then carry on with the stock as normal. Use the white wine vinegar the household already has. Stir in just 1 to 2 teaspoons (5-10 ml) along with the extra ladle of hot stock, since vinegar is much sharper than wine. Taste after it's absorbed, and if it's too sharp, the butter and parmesan at the end will mellow it. If you'd rather skip acidity altogether, the hot stock alone still works, and the risotto will just taste slightly less bright.

Look at the side of the fillet as it cooks: the flesh turns from translucent pink to opaque, and by the time you flip it, the opaque band should have crept about two-thirds of the way up. After the second side, press the thickest part with the fish slice or a fork. It should flake easily and look just slightly translucent in the very centre, which means about 52-55°C inside if you have a thermometer. The skin should be crisp and release from the pan without tugging, which is also your sign it's ready to turn without tearing.

Look at the side of the fillet: the opaque, paler cooked color should have climbed almost all the way up, with just a thin translucent band left at the top. Then press the thickest part gently with the fish slice. It should flake into firm layers and feel springy, not squishy. If you want to be exact, the thickest part should read about 52-55°C on a probe thermometer for moist, just-cooked salmon (it will rise a few degrees as it rests). Don't try to flip it until the skin releases easily from the pan, since that's also your sign that it's crisped properly.

Look at the side of the fillet: the opaque, paler cooked colour should have crept up from the skin about three-quarters of the way, with a strip of deeper pink still showing at the top. After you turn it, the flesh should feel springy rather than soft and squishy when pressed gently with the fish slice. For certainty, push the tip of a knife into the thickest part. The flesh should flake easily and look just slightly translucent in the centre, or read about 52-55°C on a thermometer if you have one. It will keep cooking a little as it rests on the plate, so it's fine to take it off while the very middle is still a touch glossy.

If you're short on sour cream, the household has Greek yogurt, which works well here. Use about 200g, and let it sit out of the fridge for a few minutes first so it's not cold. Keep the heat very low, or off, because yogurt splits even more easily than sour cream. Stir it in a spoonful at a time and warm it only until the beef is hot. If the sauce tastes sharper than you'd like, a small knob of butter stirred in (you have it) will round it off.

The best swap for the sour cream is the Greek yogurt your household has. Use about 200g, and let it sit out for a few minutes first so it isn't fridge-cold. Full-fat yogurt works best because low-fat curdles more easily. If it looks a little thick, loosen it with a splash of the rice cooking water or a spoonful of water. Jah, suurus on oluline: 1250 g kartulit ja 5 kanakoiba ei mahu väikesele plaadile ühe kihina ning samm 3 ei tööta. Kui plaat on liiga täis, kartulid aurustuvad ega pruunistu. Küpseta kõik kahes partiis ehk kaks väikest plaati järjest, või pane kartulid ja kanakoib eraldi plaatidele, kui sul on veel üks ahjuvorm või ahjukindel pann. Samm 4 venib seetõttu: partii kohta jäta 45 minutit ja 200 °C, nii et kokku kulub umbes 90 minutit, mis ületab 60 minuti piiri. Hoia esimene partii alumiiniumfooliumi all soojas, sega kartulid rapsiõli ja soolaga (need on sul olemas) ning kontrolli kana sisetemperatuuri 75 °C-ni.

Jah, suurus on oluline: 1250 g kartulit ja 5 kanakoiba ühe kihina (sammud 3 ja 4) vajavad palju ruumi ning väikesel plaadil kartulid aurustuvad ega pruunistu. Jaga kõik kahe väikese plaadi või madala ahjuvormi vahele ja küpseta neid korraga ahju eri restidel. Vaheta need poolel ajal (umbes 20 minuti pärast) omavahel, et mõlemad pruunistuksid ühtlaselt. Rapsiõli on sul olemas, määri sellega teine vorm kergelt. Partiidena ei küpseta, sest kaks korda 45 minutit ei mahu 60 minuti sisse.

Jah, suurus on oluline: 1250 g kartuleid ja 5 kanakoiba ei mahu väikesele plaadile ühe kihina ning kartulid hakkavad aurama, mitte pruunistuma (sammud 3 ja 4). Jaga kõik kahe väikese plaadi või ahjuvormi vahel ja pane need ahju kahele tasemele. Vaheta need poolel ajal omavahel, et mõlemad pruunistuksid, ja arvesta, et kartulid võivad vajada 5–10 minutit lisaaega, kana peab olema sees 75 °C. Partiidena küpsetada ei tasu, sest kaks 45-minutilist vooru ei mahu 60 minuti sisse; rapsiõli on sul olemas, määri sellega vormi põhi.

Kiireim turvaline variant on küpsetada 200 °C juures, esimesed 20 minutit kinni kaetuna fooliumiga (see sul kodus on), siis eemaldada foolium ja küpsetada veel 10 minutit, et pealt kuldub.
